changed_files.change: Replaced the REFERENCE_DEF regex scan with readReferenceDefinitions(), a linear hand-written scanner. Reading 1 reproduces the pattern exactly, including its lastIndex resume; reading 2 adds CommonMark's escape-aware label (first unescaped `]`, no unescaped `[` inside) and never moves the cursor. A key is now the label truncated at its first `]`, which is the byte string the use side produces and which keeps the cost proof's step (i) true by construction. Added REFERENCE_DESTINATION (the replaced pattern's destination tail, sticky) and LINE_TERMINATORS. Rewrote the three comments that stated the old reason for the `]` fact.

Three tests added, all RED before the change: T83#F-001 escape spellings at the detector and through the redaction, persistence and transport seams, with no-release and no-false-positive controls; T83#F-001 structural property, 125 generated labels that must all still resolve when used (the observable form of "no key contains `]`"); T83#F-001 cost, eight definition-scan shapes under the same 500 ms budget the other perf tests use.

questions.question: REFERENCE_DEF was quadratic at HEAD (24 643.6 ms at a public boundary on 704 000 bytes of `[aaaaaaaaa\n`, exponent 2.01), and the mechanism this repair needed removed it. Should that have been its own round under the scope decision's exception, and does it need an independent review pass of its own?
questions.why: It is a blocker reproduced at a public boundary, so it fires the same exception T82#F-001 fired, but declaring the exception is a reviewer/orchestrator call and not the implementer's. The removal was not optional: the alternative mechanism (a second escape-aware pattern) roughly doubles that reading, which the cost acceptance criterion forbids.

questions.question: Label matching is now an over-approximation for labels carrying a backslash escape: two labels differing only after their first `]` share a key. policies.md still says the label is matched the way CommonMark matches it. Should that sentence gain a clause and the document bump to 0.1.5?
questions.why: The dispatch permits editing the auto-fetch subsection only if the change MAKES the current wording untrue. It was already untrue before this change, in the release direction; it is now untrue in the flagging direction. The strict reading of the condition says do not edit, but the document's own discipline is to name every deviation explicitly.
